chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid al-Qammait, from Durays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, made lust ten parts: nine of them are in women and one is in men. And were it not for what God, the Mighty and Majestic, placed in them [women] of parts of modesty, equal in measure to the parts of lust, there would be nine women attached to every man.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological explanation for the difference in sexual desire between men and women in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this famous hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), illustrating the divine wisdom behind the asymmetry of sexual desire, where men possess nine parts and women one. This narration highlights the complementary nature of human psychology, positing that the modesty (*haya'*) granted to women acts as a precise counterbalance to male lust, thereby maintaining social stability and preventing excessive polygyny or chaotic attachment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-28 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Abi Khalid al-Qamat, on the authority of Zaris that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

The Blessed the Sublime God has made lust in ten parts, nine of which is in women and one is in men. Were it not for the fact that the Honorable the Exalted God has granted women as much shame as lust, there would have been nine women hanging over every man.”
